description: UK GDPR / ICO data-minimisation regex patterns. Order matters: more specific patterns (NI number, card, phone) must run before broader ones (postcode) to avoid a NI number or phone number being partially re-caught by a looser rule. Update this file to add/adjust patterns; no code changes or redeploys are required.

patterns.description: UK National Insurance Number, e.g. QQ123456C. Deliberately broader than the strict HMRC letter set (which excludes D,F,I,Q,U,V) so that the department's own worked example, QQ123456C - the standard HMRC-documented placeholder NINO used precisely because it can never be a real one - is still caught. A stricter pattern would silently miss it. Given the brief's 0% PII-leakage target, over-masking an unlikely two-letter/six-digit/suffix-letter coincidence is the safe direction; under-masking a real NINO is not. See README Design Decisions.

Credit/debit card number, 13-19 digits (covers the standard 13-16 digit range plus longer schemes some debit/prepaid cards use), optionally space/hyphen separated. Widened from the brief's literal {13,16} bound after SQL-11 (the PII assurance check) caught real 19-digit card numbers in the sample data slipping through entirely: with a trailing \b anchor, a quantifier capped at 16 can never match a token that is actually longer than 16, because the match has to end exactly at the token's true end for \b to hold. See README Design Decisions.
UK landline/mobile in national or +44 international format
UK postcode, e.g. SW1A 1AA. Run last: without the NI/phone/card patterns running first, this would also swallow fragments of those entities.
